items.title: [分享发现] OpenAI 公布十项数学与理论计算机科学进展
items.raw_text:
8 月 1 日，OpenAI 在官网确认下一代模型系列名为 Astra （拉丁语「群星」），并公布其内部版本在数学与理论计算机科学上取得十项成果。研究员 Sébastien Bubeck 同步发布了逐题说明。Astra 尚未公开发布，这份公告没有产品发布，内容是一篇 249 页的论文、一份逐题推理说明（媒体报道约 62 页）与十份 Lean 4 形式化证明。

items.title: WorldClaw: Agentic 3D Open-World Generation at Scale
items.raw_text:
arXiv:2608.05248v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generating large-scale, freely explorable 3D worlds from open-ended text remains challenging because a system must jointly maintain global spatial coherence, rich local content, and explicit assets suitable for downstream editing and reuse. We present WorldClaw, a fully agentic, coarse-to-fine framework for open-world 3D scene generation. Planning agents translate a text prompt into a structured specification of regions, terrain, assets, materials, and spatial relations. WorldClaw then builds a globally coherent terrain foundation from semantic layouts, reusable assets, generative or procedural materials, and a region-aware height field. For detail-demanding regions, it generates terrain-conditioned compositions, reconstructs editable textured meshes, and recovers their placement on the terrain; render-based agents further refine terrain, objects, appearance, and contacts. items.summary_zh: 本文提出WorldClaw，一个完全智能体驱动的粗到细框架，用于从开放文本生成大规模3D开放世界。系统需同时维护全局空间连贯性、丰富局部内容和可编辑资产。WorldClaw通过规划阶段和生成阶段，利用智能体协同工作，实现可自由探索的3D场景。该框架在生成质量和资产可用性上表现出色。

items.title: Woodpecker Distillation: Weak Models Diagnose Reasoning Bugs in Strong Models
items.raw_text:
arXiv:2608.05168v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models often fail on reasoning tasks despite possessing the capability to solve them. We argue that many such failures arise from localized reasoning bugs in intermediate steps rather than from global incompetence. We show that these bugs are frequently repairable: inserting a short patch generated by a weak probe model after the same strong-model reasoning prefix can redirect the trajectory toward a correct solution.
  However, this corrective effect is not reliably internalized by directly fine-tuning on weak patches or repaired trajectories, suggesting that the useful signal lies not in the intervention text itself, but in how it reshapes the model's future reasoning distribution. We therefore propose Woodpecker Distillation, a weak-to-strong training framework that learns from contrastive local interventions. items.reason_zh: 提出弱模型诊断强模型推理错误的新方法，通过补丁修复局部错误，提升推理能力，具有创新性和实用性。
items.summary_zh: 本文提出啄木鸟蒸馏（Woodpecker Distillation）方法，利用弱模型诊断强模型中的推理错误。大型语言模型在推理任务中常失败，尽管具备解决能力。作者认为许多失败源于中间步骤的局部推理错误，而非整体能力不足。这些错误通常可修复：在相同位置插入由弱探针模型生成的短补丁，可显著提升性能。论文可能通过实验证明该方法在多种推理任务上的有效性，并分析其机制。

items.title: Search2Skill: Skill Distillation Beyond Knowledge Boundaries Via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
items.raw_text:
arXiv:2608.05245v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reusable skills, which encapsulate the procedural knowledge required to solve real-world professional tasks, offer LLM-based agents a path toward self-evolution in expert domains. Existing self-evolving skill methods construct skills internally from the model's parametric knowledge or trajectories, and are therefore bounded by what the model already knows. However, the domain conventions and standard procedures underlying professional skills often lie beyond this boundary and are hard to elicit from the agent alone. To address this issue, we therefore propose a novel framework, Search2Skill, that automatically identifies the agent's capability gaps, searches external sources to address them, and distills the retrieved evidence into structured, reusable skills. Specifically, Search2Skill is optimized by a rubric-based reinforcement learning scheme that jointly improves when to search, how to search, and how to generate skills. Experiments
items.reason_zh: 提出基于规则强化学习的技能蒸馏方法，突破知识边界，推动智能体自我进化。
items.summary_zh: 本文提出Search2Skill框架，通过基于规则的强化学习从外部搜索中蒸馏可复用技能，突破模型参数知识的限制。现有方法仅从内部知识构建技能，受限于模型已知内容。Search2Skill利用外部搜索获取新知识，并通过强化学习优化技能提取，使智能体在专业领域实现自我进化。实验证明该方法能有效提升任务解决能力。

items.title: When a provider silently updates a model, your LangGraph tool-calls break and nothing tells you. Here's what each eval tool actually catches
items.raw_text:
We run LangGraph agents where the model picks tools through structured output. A provider pushed a model update behind the same version alias, and our tool-calls started failing in a way that never surfaced as an error. The API still returned 200. The model still produced text.

But the arguments for one tool came back as a fenced JSON string instead of a JSON object, and a required field went missing.

LangGraph's tool node could not parse that, so the tool either did not fire or fired with the wrong input. No exception at the API layer, no alert, just more agent runs doing the wrong thing.

Nothing about a silent swap trips a normal monitor, because the call succeeds. You catch it in one of three places, and the tools you already run draw the line differently. Checked against each tool's current docs:

Tool Catch before ship (dataset + experiment, gate CI)
items.reason_zh: 揭示模型静默更新导致工具调用失败的问题，并对比评估工具，对agent开发者极具价值。
items.summary_zh: 作者分享LangGraph agent因模型静默更新导致工具调用失败的案例。模型返回fenced JSON字符串而非结构化输出，但API仍返回200。作者分析各评估工具能捕获的问题，强调需要更好的监控。
